one_line: A French company major and a Carnatic prince-general facing off at the Battle of the Adyar, 1746.

appearance.age_look: Paradis appears late 30s, compact and athletic; Mahfuz Khan appears mid-30s to early 40s, tall and broad-shouldered.
appearance.face: Paradis has a narrow oval face, fair but sun-browned complexion, sharp nose, trimmed dark moustache, a faint old scar on his left cheek and steady, focused eyes with a calm, calculating default expression; Mahfuz Khan has a strong oval face, warm brown complexion, neatly groomed full moustache with a short beard along the jawline, prominent nose and dark, intense eyes with a dignified, resolute default expression.
appearance.hair: Paradis’s dark brown hair is tied back in a low queue just below the nape, peeking from under a black tricorn hat with a narrow gold braid edge; Mahfuz Khan’s black hair is gathered under a white, neatly wrapped South Indian-Muslim style turban (paghdi) with a subtle gold border and a small central emerald-green jewel at the front.
appearance.costume: Paradis wears a mid-18th-century French Compagnie des Indes-style officer’s coat: a knee-length dark navy wool coat with red facings, gold trim along the front edges and cuffs, brass buttons, and plain shoulder straps, over a white linen shirt with a modest collar and a cream waistcoat; he has buff-coloured knee-length breeches, white stockings, and black leather shoes with small brass buckles, plus a simple brown leather crossbelt with a cartridge box and a narrow sword belt, his look finished with a plain dark leather gauntlet glove on his left hand; Mahfuz Khan wears an ankle-length, long-sleeved cotton angarkha-style coat in rich deep green with a wrap-over front tied at the right, subtle woven floral motifs in darker green, and a broad golden-yellow sash (patka) wrapped firmly around his waist, over cream-coloured churidar trousers and soft brown leather mojari shoes; over his angarkha he wears a sleeveless, slightly flared quilted armour vest (zarbaft) in muted steel-grey with simple stitched patterns, and his forearms are covered with plain brown leather bracers, with a discreet string of prayer beads around his left wrist.
appearance.signature: Paradis carries a polished steel infantry officer’s smallsword with a plain brass hilt and simple knuckle-bow, sheathed in a dark brown leather scabbard at his left hip, while Mahfuz Khan carries a gently curved Indo-Persian talwar with a steel blade, traditional disc pommel, and a dark red leather-wrapped scabbard hanging from his golden-yellow sash on his left side.

ref_desc: Louis Paradis is a compact late-30s French officer with a sun-browned oval face, dark queue, black tricorn, navy coat with red facings, buff breeches and a brass-hilt smallsword, beside Mahfuz Khan, a tall brown-complexioned prince in a white turban, green angarkha, grey quilted vest, cream churidar and talwar in a dark red scabbard, all in navy, deep green, golden yellow, cream and dark red tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two fixed characters standing side by side: Louis Paradis and Mahfuz Khan, as historically grounded figures from the First Carnatic War near the Adyar River, 1746. Paradis is a compact, athletic French officer in his late 30s with a sun-browned oval face, small trimmed dark moustache, a faint scar on his left cheek and steady, focused eyes; his dark brown hair is tied back in a low queue under a black tricorn hat edged with narrow gold braid. He wears a knee-length dark navy wool officer’s coat with red facings, simple gold trim along the front edges and cuffs, and brass buttons, over a white linen shirt and a cream waistcoat, with buff knee-length breeches, white stockings and black leather shoes with small brass buckles; add a brown leather crossbelt with a cartridge box and a narrow sword belt, and a dark leather gauntlet glove on his left hand. His signature weapon is a polished steel infantry smallsword with a plain brass hilt and knuckle-bow, in a dark brown leather scabbard at his left hip. Beside him, Mahfuz Khan is tall and broad-shouldered, mid-30s to early 40s, with a warm brown complexion, strong oval face, neatly groomed full moustache and short beard, prominent nose and dignified, intense eyes; his black hair is covered by a white, neatly wrapped South Indian-Muslim style turban with a subtle gold border and a small emerald-green jewel at the front. He wears an ankle-length, long-sleeved deep green cotton angarkha coat with a wrap-over front tied at the right and subtle woven floral motifs, over cream churidar trousers and brown leather mojari shoes; a broad golden-yellow sash (patka) is wrapped around his waist, over which sits a sleeveless, slightly flared quilted armour vest in muted steel-grey with stitched patterns, plus plain brown leather forearm bracers and a discreet string of prayer beads at his left wrist. His signature weapon is a gently curved steel talwar with a traditional disc pommel in a dark red leather-wrapped scabbard hanging from his sash at his left side. Use a coherent palette dominated by navy blue, deep green, golden yellow, cream and dark red, and show them in neutral, balanced poses so their face shapes, hairstyles, garments, and weapons are clearly visible for consistent redrawing.
